chunks: And a group informed us, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh and Abu Abdillah al-Husayn ibn Ali, his brother, that they said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Aswad (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) asked me, after the death of Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari (may his spirit be pure), to ask Abu al-Qasim al-Ruhi (may Allah purify his spirit) to ask our Master, the Master of the Age (peace be upon him), to pray to Allah that He grant him a son (a male).

He said: So I asked him, and he conveyed that request. Then he informed me three days later that the Imam had prayed for Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah have mercy on him), that a blessed son would be born to him whom Allah would benefit from, and after him other sons. Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Aswad said: I asked him regarding my own self, that he pray for me that I be granted a son (a male). He did not reply affirmatively to me and said to me: 'There is no way for this to happen.' He said: So, for Ali ibn al-Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him), his son Muhammad ibn Ali was born that year, and after him other sons, but no son was born to me.

Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh said: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Aswad would often say to me, when he saw me going to the session of our Shaykh Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) and showing desire for the books of knowledge and memorizing them: 'It is not surprising that you have this desire for knowledge, for you were born through the supplication of the Imam (peace be upon him).'.

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ الرُّوحِيُّ: Abu al-Qasim al-Ruhi (a prominent deputy of the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the Imam's prayer for the birth of Ibn Babawayh's son?
ai.summary: This narrative from Kitab al-Ghayba highlights the spiritual authority of the Imam of the Age in granting specific divine favors, contrasting the successful supplication for a son for Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh with the narrator's own distinct destiny. It underscores the Shia belief that the Imam's prayers directly influence the lineage and intellectual capacities of the learned class, linking the narrator's passion for hadith scholarship to his birth through the Imam's intercession.
